title: Can revocation persist without becoming a profile?
question: Can TurtleBlock AI carry a project-scoped learner revocation across session boundaries so an old purpose stays quiet, while refusing to turn that authority state into a generalized personal preference or identity model?
why_now: Initiative Authority is now semantically testable for one transition. Too little persistence can resurrect old purpose; too much can turn a project rule into generalized state.
possible_possibles: Persist explicit project directives, not broad preferences.
Preserve revocation and explicit restoration as separate events.
Test session-boundary resurrection before runtime persistence.
x_factor: whoooo knooooowwwssssssssssss — what if the most intelligent thing persistence can remember is a boundary that tells it what not to bring back?
constraints: Do not infer revocation or restoration.
Remembered purpose cannot silently reactivate removed authority.

ontology_mappings.rationale: Revocation and restoration alter later cycles.
Directive, state, purpose, and restoration remain distinct.

ctc_mappings.rationale: Questions gain no permanent resurfacing right.

ctc_mappings.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With

ctc_mappings.rationale: Authority behavior is not learning proof.
Learners can inspect why purpose stayed quiet or returned.
Persistence carries power over whose purposes travel forward.

uncaptured_residue.observation: Remembering a boundary may differ from remembering a preference.

wait_a_minute_connection.summary: Noticing is not interruption; ask formation is not surfacing; branch difference is not application; remembered purpose is not resurrection authority.
wait_a_minute_connection.uncertainty: May be engineering rather than ontology.
